apps.title: Local AI (Ollama + Open-WebUI)
apps.description:
Local LLM inference via Ollama with Open-WebUI as the chat front-end.
Runs on CPU by default; opt-in NVIDIA GPU passthrough via the 'gpu'
compose profile (requires the gpu-nvidia host role, TBD).
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/ai
#
# Ollama (local LLM runner) + Open-WebUI (chat frontend).
#
# CPU is the default. NVIDIA GPU passthrough is opt-in via the 'gpu'
# compose profile:
#   ./scripts/up.sh --gpu core ai
#
# The two ollama variants use distinct container names; both register
# the `ollama` network alias on aurora_net so Open-WebUI always resolves
# it. Run ONE at a time (see README).

name: aurora-ai

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  # CPU inference (default). Runs unless --gpu is passed to up.sh, which
  # switches on the 'gpu' profile and drops 'cpu' so only one Ollama
  # binds :11434.
  ollama-cpu:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    container_name: ollama-cpu
    hostname: ollama
    restart: unless-stopped
    profiles: ["cpu"]
    networks:
      aurora_net:
        aliases: [ollama]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=${OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE:-5m}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/ai/ollama:/root/.ollama
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"

  ollama-gpu:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    container_name: ollama-gpu
    hostname: ollama
    restart: unless-stopped
    profiles: ["gpu"]
    networks:
      aurora_net:
        aliases: [ollama]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=${OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE:-5m}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/ai/ollama:/root/.ollama
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: all
              capabilities: [gpu]

  open-webui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    container_name: open-webui
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434
      - WEBUI_SECRET_KEY=${WEBUI_SECRET_KEY}
      - DEFAULT_MODELS=${DEFAULT_MODELS:-}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/ai/open-webui:/app/backend/data
    ports:
      - "3011:8080"
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/ai / .env.example
#
# Copy to .env and fill in.

TZ=Europe/London

# ---- Ollama ----
# How long to keep a loaded model warm in RAM/VRAM between requests.
# Increase for a "chat" workflow, decrease to free memory faster.
OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=5m

# ---- Open-WebUI ----
# Signing key for session tokens. Any long random string.
#   openssl rand -hex 32
WEBUI_SECRET_KEY=

# Comma-separated list of models to preselect in the UI dropdown.
# Models still have to be pulled first (`ollama pull <name>`).
#   e.g. llama3.2,qwen2.5-coder:7b,mistral-nemo
DEFAULT_MODELS=
apps.readme:
# ai

Local LLM inference: **Ollama** (model runtime) + **Open-WebUI** (chat
frontend).

## First-run

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`. Set `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY` (generate with
   `openssl rand -hex 32`).
2. `./scripts/up.sh core ai`
3. Open-WebUI: `https://ai.$DOMAIN/` — first user to sign up
   becomes the admin.
4. Pull a model:
   ```
   docker exec -it ollama-cpu ollama pull llama3.2
   docker exec -it ollama-cpu ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b
   ```
   (For GPU: replace `ollama-cpu` with `ollama-gpu`.)

## RAM / VRAM guidance

Quantised (Q4) models, rough rule of thumb:

| Model size | Fits in            | Typical use                 |
|------------|--------------------|-----------------------------|
| 1B–3B      | ~4 GB              | quick chat, embeddings      |
| 7B–8B      | ~8 GB              | coding assist (qwen-coder)  |
| 13B        | ~16 GB             | general chat, higher quality|
| 32B–34B    | ~24 GB             | high quality reasoning      |
| 70B        | ~48 GB (GPU only)  | best quality, needs 2× 3090 |

CPU inference is fine for 1B–8B on a modern desktop; expect 5–20 tok/s.
GPU is 5–20× faster.

## GPU passthrough (opt-in)

The `gpu` compose profile brings up an `ollama-gpu` container that
reserves all NVIDIA GPUs on the host.

**Prerequisites (host):**
- NVIDIA driver installed
- NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed and Docker restarted:
  `sudo apt install nvidia-container-toolkit && sudo systemctl restart docker`

**Enabling:**
```
docker stop ollama-cpu   # only one ollama can bind :11434
./scripts/up.sh --gpu core ai
```

Both variants share the `../../data/ai/ollama` volume so pulled models
carry over. Both register `ollama` as a network alias, so Open-WebUI's
`OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434` works unchanged.

**Note:** The `gpu-nvidia` host role referenced in `manifest.yml` does
not yet exist in `host/roles/`. Until it does, install the NVIDIA
Container Toolkit manually.

## Ports

See `manifest.yml`.

apps.title: Backup (Kopia)
apps.description:
Kopia is a deduplicating, encrypted backup tool with a friendly web
UI. Defaults to a local filesystem repository under
data/backup/repository; can be reconfigured to point at B2, S3, GCS,
Azure, SFTP or WebDAV from the UI without changing this package.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/backup
#
# Kopia is a repository-based deduplicating backup tool with a decent
# web UI. Runs in "server" mode; you connect to it via the browser and
# drive snapshots from there, or shell in and use the `kopia` CLI.
#
# Two bind mounts to be aware of:
#   /data       -> host / (read-only). Kopia never writes here.
#   /repository -> data/backup/repository. Local filesystem repo by
#                  default. To back up to B2/S3 instead, leave this
#                  unused and reconfigure the repo from inside the UI
#                  (or via `kopia repository create s3 ...`).

name: aurora-backup

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  kopia:
    image: kopia/kopia:latest
    container_name: kopia
    hostname: kopia
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    # Kopia's server mode. Bind to 0.0.0.0 inside the container; Caddy
    # (or a LAN port) does the exposure. Basic auth is set via
    # KOPIA_UI_USER/PASSWORD env vars. --without-password used to sit in
    # this list and kopia rejected the whole config with "listen address
    # not allowed for insecure server without password" — that flag
    # disables the SERVER-side basic auth we just configured on the two
    # lines above, and kopia refuses to publish an unauthenticated HTTP
    # API on anything other than loopback. Removed 2026-08-27 during the
    # QA-sweep fixes.
    command:
      - server
      - start
      - --insecure
      - --address=0.0.0.0:51515
      - --server-username=${KOPIA_UI_USER:-admin}
      - --server-password=${KOPIA_UI_PASSWORD:-changeme}
      - --ui
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      # Consumed by kopia CLI on first `repository create` / `connect`.
      - KOPIA_PASSWORD=${KOPIA_PASSWORD:-}
      # Optional remote repo hints — see .env.example.
      - KOPIA_REPOSITORY=${KOPIA_REPOSITORY:-}
    volumes:
      # Persistent kopia server + client config.
      - ../../data/backup/kopia:/app/config
      - ../../data/backup/cache:/app/cache
      - ../../data/backup/logs:/app/logs
      # Local filesystem repository (default). If you switch to B2/S3
      # you can leave this mounted; it just won't be used.
      - ../../data/backup/repository:/repository
      # Everything Kopia is allowed to snapshot from. Read-only for
      # safety — Kopia is a backup tool, it should never mutate host
      # files. Exclude patterns live in policies/default-policy.json.
      - /:/data:ro
    ports:
      - "51515:51515"
apps.env_example:
# Copy to .env and fill in.
#
# Every KEY substituted in compose.yml is listed here.

TZ=Europe/London

# ---- Kopia server UI auth ----
# The web UI is protected with HTTP basic auth. Change both.
KOPIA_UI_USER=admin
KOPIA_UI_PASSWORD=changeme

# ---- Repository encryption password ----
# This is the password that unlocks the repository. NEVER change this
# after `kopia repository create`; if you lose it, backups are gone.
# Store a copy in a password manager AND print a paper copy.
KOPIA_PASSWORD=

# ---- Optional: remote repository ------------------------------------
# Only set KOPIA_REPOSITORY if you want the CLI to auto-connect to a
# remote repo on start. When unset (default), the UI drives repo
# creation and connection.
#
# Examples (uncomment ONE):
#
#   Backblaze B2:
# KOPIA_REPOSITORY=b2 --bucket=aurora-backups --key-id=... --key=...
#
#   Amazon S3 / MinIO / R2 / etc.:
# KOPIA_REPOSITORY=s3 --bucket=aurora-backups --endpoint=s3.amazonaws.com --access-key=... --secret-access-key=...
#
#   SFTP to another home server:
# KOPIA_REPOSITORY=sftp --path=/backups/aurora --host=nas.local --username=backup --keyfile=/app/config/id_ed25519
#
#   Local filesystem (default; already mounted at /repository):
# KOPIA_REPOSITORY=filesystem --path=/repository
KOPIA_REPOSITORY=
apps.readme:
# backup

Kopia-based backups with a web UI, encrypted at rest, deduplicated.

## Repository

**Default:** local filesystem at `data/backup/repository/` on this
host. Useful for testing but does not protect you from disk loss —
plan to swap to a remote target as soon as you're happy.

**Remote (recommended):** point Kopia at Backblaze B2, S3, R2, GCS,
Azure, SFTP or WebDAV. Two ways to configure:

1. **From the UI** (easiest): open `https://backup.$DOMAIN/`,
   click **Reconnect** → pick provider, paste creds.
2. **Auto-connect on start**: set `KOPIA_REPOSITORY` in `.env` to a
   full CLI arg string (see `.env.example` for examples for B2/S3/SFTP).

## What to back up

Kopia sees the whole host at `/data` (read-only). Snapshot sources
worth adding on day one:

| Path (inside container)           | Why                             |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| `/data/home/<user>/aurora.local/group_vars/all.yml` | machine identity |
| `/data/home/<user>/aurora.local/packages/*/.env`    | all secrets      |
| `/data/home/<user>/aurora.local/data/*/config`      | per-app configs  |
| `/data/home/<user>/aurora.local/data/caddy`         | root CA & certs  |
| `/data/etc`                                       | host config      |

**EXCLUDED** by the default policy (`policies/default-policy.json`):

- `**/media/*` (movies/TV/downloads — reproducible, huge)
- `**/data/*/cache`
- `**/data/*/logs`
- `**/node_modules`, `**/.git/objects`
- `**/.cache`, `**/.local/share/Trash`

## First-run

1. `cp .env.example .env`; fill in `KOPIA_UI_PASSWORD` and
   `KOPIA_PASSWORD` (write it down — losing it means losing the repo).
2. `./scripts/up.sh backup`
3. Open `https://backup.$DOMAIN/`. If unconfigured, click
   **Create Repository** → **Filesystem** → path `/repository`,
   encryption password = `KOPIA_PASSWORD`.
4. Add snapshot sources from the list above.
5. Import `policies/default-policy.json` as a starting policy for the
   global default.
6. Set a schedule (nightly is a good start).

## Ports

See `manifest.yml`.

## Integration

- `caddy.snippet` fronts the UI on `backup.$DOMAIN` with a
  second basic-auth layer (defence in depth over Kopia's own auth).
- `homepage.yml` adds a Kopia tile with status widget.

apps.title: Bulwark (webmail)
apps.description:
Bulwark is a self-hosted webmail suite (mail + calendar + contacts +
files) built for the JMAP protocol and Stalwart. A front end only — the
mail server (Stalwart) lives in the core stack; this connects to it over
JMAP on aurora_net. Alternative to Roundcube in the `webmail` group;
Roundcube remains the default.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/bulwark
#
# Bulwark webmail — a front end only. The mail server (Stalwart) lives
# in packages/core; this connects to it over JMAP on aurora_net. An
# alternative to Roundcube in the `webmail` variant group (SnappyMail is
# the third option). See the upstream README for the wizard/config story:
# https://github.com/bulwarkmail/webmail.
#
# Bind-mount source paths resolve against packages/core/ (the first -f
# file), NOT this directory — see docs/PACKAGE_CONTRACT.md. Hence
# ../../data/bulwark/... rather than ./data.

name: aurora-bulwark

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  bulwark:
    # Upstream ships a `latest` tag alongside semver tags on GHCR. Pinned
    # to the current tagged release for reproducibility; bump by hand and
    # regenerate pins.env when a new one lands.
    image: ghcr.io/bulwarkmail/webmail:${BULWARK_VERSION:-1.9.2}
    container_name: bulwark
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      # Bulwark listens on this addr:port inside the container. Kept at
      # upstream defaults; nothing else on aurora_net expects to reach
      # bulwark:3000 by any other name.
      - HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
      - PORT=3000
      # Point Bulwark straight at Stalwart's JMAP endpoint on aurora_net.
      # Stalwart serves JMAP + admin UI on :8080 (see packages/core). The
      # webmail's JMAP client runs server-side in Next.js, so it can use
      # the internal service name rather than the Authelia-gated
      # mail-admin.$DOMAIN vhost. Setting this env var also skips the
      # first-run setup wizard for the JMAP URL field.
      - JMAP_SERVER_URL=${BULWARK_JMAP_URL:-http://stalwart:8080}
      # Turns on Stalwart-specific integrations (password change, Sieve
      # filter editor, etc.) — safe to leave on because core always runs
      # Stalwart.
      - STALWART_FEATURES=true
      # Session cookie key. Generated by the setup wizard on first boot
      # if left blank; rotate-secrets.sh can also pre-seed it in .env.
      - SESSION_SECRET=${BULWARK_SESSION_SECRET:-}
    volumes:
      # Encrypted per-user settings (SETTINGS_DATA_DIR).
      - ../../data/bulwark/settings:/app/data/settings
      # Admin-authored config: config.json, policy.json, admin password
      # hash, plugins, themes, branding uploads (ADMIN_CONFIG_DIR). Can be
      # remounted :ro after the wizard finishes.
      - ../../data/bulwark/admin:/app/data/admin
      # Admin runtime state: audit log, setup token, login timestamps
      # (ADMIN_STATE_DIR). Always read-write.
      - ../../data/bulwark/admin-state:/app/data/admin-state
      # Anonymous telemetry consent + instance id (TELEMETRY_DATA_DIR).
      # Telemetry is off by default; the volume just preserves the "off"
      # choice across upgrades.
      - ../../data/bulwark/telemetry:/app/data/telemetry
    # No host port on purpose. Bulwark serves on :3000, reachable only via
    # Caddy at bulwark.$DOMAIN — which is gated by Authelia (see manifest
    # sso:). Publishing a host port here would let any LAN device reach
    # the webmail directly and walk straight around the Authelia gate.
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/bulwark / .env.example
#
# Copy to .env and edit. Every value has a working default; the file is
# here so operators can pin a version or override the JMAP endpoint
# without editing compose.yml.

# Bulwark image tag on ghcr.io/bulwarkmail/webmail. Upstream ships semver
# tags plus a rolling `latest`; pinned in compose.yml for reproducibility.
BULWARK_VERSION=1.9.2

# Where Bulwark reaches Stalwart's JMAP endpoint. Default targets the
# internal service name on aurora_net, so it bypasses the Authelia gate
# on mail-admin.$DOMAIN — the JMAP client runs server-side in Next.js and
# does not need the public hostname. Override only if you're pointing
# Bulwark at a Stalwart instance somewhere else on the network.
BULWARK_JMAP_URL=http://stalwart:8080

# Session cookie signing key (AES-256-GCM). If left blank, Bulwark's
# first-run setup wizard generates and stores one in data/bulwark/admin/;
# set it here if you'd rather manage the secret yourself (rotate-secrets.sh
# treats anything >=12 chars as populated). Generate with:
#   openssl rand -base64 32
BULWARK_SESSION_SECRET=
apps.readme:
# bulwark (webmail)

[Bulwark](https://github.com/bulwarkmail/webmail) is a self-hosted webmail
suite (mail, calendar, contacts, files) built for the [JMAP](https://jmap.io)
protocol and [Stalwart](https://stalw.art/). It is a **front end only**:
the mail server (Stalwart) lives in the core stack, and Bulwark connects
to it over JMAP on the internal `aurora_net`. It is an alternative in the
`webmail` variant group; Roundcube remains the default, SnappyMail is the
lighter-weight third option.

Bulwark is a Next.js/Node app — heavier at runtime than Roundcube's PHP,
but it speaks JMAP natively (Stalwart's first-class protocol) and rolls
mail + calendar + contacts + files into one login.

## First-run

1. **Create a mailbox on the mail server first.** Bulwark has no accounts
   of its own — it authenticates against Stalwart. Add one via the
   Stalwart admin UI at `https://mail-admin.$DOMAIN/` (or its API).
2. `cp packages/bulwark/.env.example packages/bulwark/.env` (optional;
   every value has a working default).
3. `./scripts/up.sh core bulwark`
4. Visit `https://bulwark.$DOMAIN/` and complete Bulwark's own web-based
   setup wizard: accept the pre-filled JMAP endpoint
   (`http://stalwart:8080` — Bulwark reaches Stalwart internally on
   `aurora_net`), set an admin password, and finish.
5. Sign in with the full mailbox address and its password.

## Two logins, by design

`bulwark.$DOMAIN` is gated behind Authelia (`sso: protect: true`).
Reaching the inbox is two steps:

1. **Authelia** — sign in as an Aurora user (password + 2FA).
2. **Bulwark** — sign in to the mailbox with its JMAP password.

They are not redundant: Authelia authenticates *the person* (and hides
the webmail from any unauthenticated LAN device), while Bulwark needs the
actual mailbox password to open the JMAP session. True single-login would
need Stalwart to trust Authelia's tokens as its directory, which makes
Stalwart reject inbound mail to any address that hasn't logged in yet —
not a trade worth making for a mail server. Bulwark also has native
OAuth2/OIDC support, so an operator who wants one-login here can point
Bulwark's `OAUTH_*` settings at Authelia later; the default keeps the
same convention as Roundcube/SnappyMail.

## Internal JMAP to Stalwart

Bulwark's JMAP client runs server-side in Next.js, so it can reach
Stalwart on the internal service name (`http://stalwart:8080`) without
going back out through Caddy. That means it bypasses the Authelia gate on
`mail-admin.$DOMAIN` (fine — the request never leaves aurora_net) and it
does not need to trust Stalwart's internal certificate (there's no TLS on
the hop). Override with `BULWARK_JMAP_URL` in `packages/bulwark/.env` if
you point Bulwark at a Stalwart running somewhere else.

## Storage

`data/bulwark/` holds four things:

- `settings/` — per-user preferences (encrypted).
- `admin/` — operator-authored config (config.json, policy.json, admin
  password hash, plugins, themes, branding uploads). Can be remounted
  read-only after the setup wizard completes.
- `admin-state/` — runtime state (audit log, setup token, login
  timestamps).
- `telemetry/` — anonymous telemetry consent + a stable instance id.
  Telemetry is off by default.

The mail itself is Stalwart's, under `data/stalwart/`, and is backed up
by core. The manifest's `backup:` block keeps the settings, admin config
and audit log so they survive a rebuild.

## Ports

None on the host. The webmail is reachable only via Caddy at
`bulwark.$DOMAIN`, behind Authelia — a published port would bypass that
gate on the LAN. The mail protocol ports (25/143/465/587/993) and the
JMAP endpoint on :8080 belong to Stalwart in core.

apps.title: Core (dashboard + reverse proxy)
apps.description:
Always on. Caddy is the single entry point on :80/:443 and fans out
to every other package on subdomains under $DOMAIN. Aurora
(packages/dashboard) is the dashboard, reachable at the apex domain.
Authelia provides SSO + 2FA from Day 0: the auth.$DOMAIN portal and
the reusable (authelia) forward-auth route live here, and any package
declaring `sso.protect: true` is gated behind it.
Stalwart is the box's mail server (SMTP/IMAP/JMAP), always present so
the system can send and receive mail; its admin UI sits behind Authelia
at mail-admin.$DOMAIN. Webmail frontends live in their own packages.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/core
#
# Always on. Caddy is the single entry point on :80/:443 and fans out
# to every other package on subdomains under $DOMAIN. Aurora itself
# (packages/dashboard) is the landing page at the apex $DOMAIN.
#
# Depends on the external network `aurora_net` (see scripts/up.sh which
# creates it once).

name: aurora-core

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2-alpine
    container_name: caddy
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    # 2026-08-03: `--watch` makes Caddy re-read the Caddyfile (and every
    # snippet imported via `import /etc/caddy/snippets/*.caddy`) on any
    # change, without needing an external `caddy reload` call. Solves the
    # "enabled the notes package, snippet was rendered, but Caddy is still
    # serving stale routes" trap Bruce hit when notes.aurora.local returned
    # an empty 200 despite everything else being wired.
    #
    # Alternative approaches, documented for a follow-up if `--watch` ever
    # proves too aggressive (it re-parses on ANY file event; heavy edits
    # can double-reload):
    #   A. LaunchService (Java backend) shells out `docker exec caddy caddy
    #      reload` after materialising snippets. Explicit, scoped to real
    #      enable/disable transitions, but adds a docker.sock hop.
    #   B. Systemd path unit / inotifywait sidecar that debounces file
    #      events and triggers a reload only on stable settling. Adds
    #      moving parts.
    #   C. (this) Caddy's own `--watch` flag. Zero extra process, but
    #      Caddy's own re-parse cost on every fsevent.
    # Ship (C) now, keep A + B as scratchpad followups.
    command: caddy run --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile --watch
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
      - "443:443/udp"
    healthcheck:
      # Fast Caddy-answered path; keeps the healthcheck green even when
      # the aurora upstream is briefly restarting. See caddy/Caddyfile.
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1/caddy-health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 3
    environment:
      - DOMAIN=${DOMAIN:-aurora.local}
    extra_hosts:
      # So Caddy can reach services running in host netns (e.g. minidlna).
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    volumes:
      - ./caddy/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - ../../data/caddy/snippets:/etc/caddy/snippets:ro
      - ../../data/caddy/data:/data
      - ../../data/caddy/config:/config
      - ../../data/caddy/logs:/var/log/caddy

  # Authelia — SSO + 2FA, part of core so every fresh box has SSO live
  # from Day 0. Sits behind Caddy on auth.${DOMAIN} and integrates with
  # other packages via forward-auth: any package whose manifest declares
  # `sso.protect: true` gets `import authelia` injected into its vhost by
  # CaddySnippetService. The (authelia) named route + auth.${DOMAIN} vhost
  # live in packages/core/caddy.snippet.
  #
  # Backend: file-based users_database.yml + local SQLite. The dashboard
  # projects its own admin users into the users db via
  # AutheliaService.reconcile(). The apex dashboard vhost is deliberately
  # NOT behind Authelia (configuration.yml access_control bypasses it), so
  # the admin is never locked out of the control plane.
  authelia:
    image: authelia/authelia:latest
    container_name: authelia
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    ports:
      # Bound only for local debugging. Real access is via Caddy on
      # https://auth.${DOMAIN}. Comment out to hide from the LAN.
      - "127.0.0.1:9091:9091"
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      # configuration.yml uses Go template syntax ({{ env "..." }}) to
      # pull in DOMAIN and the secrets below. Authelia only evaluates
      # that syntax with this filter enabled — without it the literal
      # "{{ env ... }}" string reaches the YAML parser and every
      # templated field fails validation.
      - X_AUTHELIA_CONFIG_FILTERS=template
      # Deliberately NOT named AUTHELIA_JWT_SECRET inside the
      # container. That exact name is on Authelia's own fixed list of
      # legacy "environment secret" variables, which it auto-maps onto
      # the deprecated top-level jwt_secret key with no template
      # filter involved at all — a second, independent mechanism
      # acting on the same value as configuration.yml's own
      # identity_validation.reset_password.jwt_secret template below.
      # Having both present (even with identical values) makes
      # Authelia refuse to start: it declines to reconcile the two and
      # the new key ends up unset ("option 'jwt_secret' is required").
      # Renaming only what the container sees avoids the collision;
      # packages/core/.env, .env.example, manifest.yml and
      # IdentitySecretsService all keep calling it AUTHELIA_JWT_SECRET
      # — this is the one place that value is handed to Authelia under
      # a different name.
      - AURORA_IDENTITY_JWT_SECRET=${AUTHELIA_JWT_SECRET}
      # Session secret and storage encryption key don't have the above
      # problem — Authelia's auto-mapping target for both is the
      # current, non-deprecated key (session.secret / storage.
      # encryption_key), the same one configuration.yml's template
      # writes to, so the two mechanisms agree rather than collide.
      - AUTHELIA_SESSION_SECRET=${AUTHELIA_SESSION_SECRET}
      - AUTHELIA_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${AUTHELIA_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      # Bake the domain into cookies via env; configuration.yml
      # references ${DOMAIN}.
      - DOMAIN=${DOMAIN:-aurora.local}
      # Optional SMTP notifier vars. Authelia maps any
      # AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_* env var straight onto notifier.smtp.*,
      # even if the value is empty, and having both notifier.smtp and
      # notifier.filesystem present at once is a fatal config error.
      # These bare entries (no "=value") are Compose's shell-passthrough
      # form: the variable is forwarded only if it's actually set in
      # the shell that invokes `docker compose`, and otherwise it is
      # genuinely absent from the container rather than present-but-
      # empty. up.sh sources packages/core/.env into its own shell
      # before calling compose, so uncommenting one of these five lines
      # in .env is what makes it appear here; leaving them commented (the
      # default, filesystem notifier) means bash's `.` never defines the
      # shell variable in the first place, so it stays truly unset.
      - AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_HOST
      - AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_PORT
      - AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_USERNAME
      - AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_PASSWORD
      - AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_SENDER
    volumes:
      - ./authelia:/config:ro
      # State (SQLite, notifications). Users db lives here too so it
      # can be edited without a rebuild.
      - ../../data/authelia:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "--tries=1", "--timeout=5", "http://127.0.0.1:9091/api/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 15s

  # Stalwart — all-in-one mail server (SMTP/IMAP/JMAP) in one Rust binary,
  # no Postfix/Dovecot/Rspamd sidecars. In core so the box always has a
  # mail substrate: system notifications, and the future agent/secretary,
  # can rely on it being present like storage.
  #
  # Webmail is deliberately NOT here — the frontends (Roundcube,
  # SnappyMail) are their own variant packages that connect to this over
  # IMAP on aurora_net. Stalwart's own HTTP (admin UI + JMAP) is proxied
  # by Caddy at mail-admin.${DOMAIN}, gated to admins (see caddy.snippet).
  stalwart:
    image: stalwartlabs/stalwart:v0.16
    container_name: stalwart
    restart: unless-stopped
    hostname: ${MAIL_HOSTNAME:-mail.aurora.local}
    networks: [aurora_net]
    # Mail protocols on the host — Caddy is HTTP-only and cannot proxy
    # these. Native clients (Apple Mail, Thunderbird, phones) and inbound
    # server-to-server SMTP reach Stalwart directly with the mailbox
    # credential. POP3 (110/995) left off; IMAP is the default. Stalwart's
    # HTTP (admin/JMAP) is NOT published — Caddy reaches it on :8080 over
    # aurora_net, so it never fights Caddy for :443.
    ports:
      - "25:25"       # inbound SMTP / MX
      - "143:143"     # IMAP (STARTTLS)
      - "465:465"     # submission, implicit TLS
      - "587:587"     # submission, STARTTLS
      - "993:993"     # IMAPS
      - "4190:4190"   # ManageSieve
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      # Declarative bootstrap: seed the recovery admin rather than scraping
      # the first-boot log for temporary credentials. Add STALWART_ADMIN_SECRET
      # to packages/core/.env so rotate-secrets.sh generates a real one; the
      # default below only exists so a fresh testbed boots — change it.
      - STALWART_RECOVERY_ADMIN=admin:${STALWART_ADMIN_SECRET:-aurora-change-me}
    volumes:
      # v0.16: a tiny JSON at /etc/stalwart describes only the datastore;
      # everything else lives in the DB, edited via the admin UI/API. One
      # data directory under /var/lib/stalwart — the whole backup surface.
      - ../../data/stalwart/etc:/etc/stalwart
      - ../../data/stalwart/lib:/var/lib/stalwart

  # Homepage retired in v0.1 — Aurora is the single landing page.
  # If you want the tile-grid dashboard back, restore this block and
  # re-add the $DOMAIN vhost in packages/core/caddy/Caddyfile.
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/core / .env
#
# Copy to .env in this directory and fill in.
#
#   cp .env.example .env
#
# HOMEPAGE_VAR_* are substituted into homepage/config/services.yaml via
# Homepage's built-in {{HOMEPAGE_VAR_FOO}} templating. Blank values will
# just show as auth errors on the tile widget; safe to leave empty until
# the service is up and you can grab a key.

# ---- Homepage / global ----
TZ=Europe/London
DOMAIN=aurora.local

# ---- Authelia SSO (REQUIRED) ---------------------------------------
# Authelia is part of core and runs on every box. These three secrets
# are auto-generated on first `scripts/up.sh` by scripts/rotate-secrets.sh
# (and belt-and-braces by IdentitySecretsService on backend boot), so a
# fresh install needs no manual step. To set them by hand:
#   openssl rand -hex 32
AUTHELIA_JWT_SECRET=
AUTHELIA_SESSION_SECRET=
AUTHELIA_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY=

# ---- Authelia notifier / SMTP (OPTIONAL) ---------------------------
# Commented out on purpose. compose.yml forwards these via shell
# passthrough, which only passes a key that's actually present here.
# Authelia treats the mere presence of an AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_* env
# var as "SMTP is configured", even blank, and having both
# notifier.smtp and notifier.filesystem configured at once is a fatal
# error. Uncomment and fill in all five to switch to SMTP; leave them
# commented for the filesystem notifier (2FA/reset links land in
# data/authelia/notification.txt on the host).
# AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_HOST=
# AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_PORT=587
# AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_USERNAME=
# AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_PASSWORD=
# AUTHELIA_NOTIFIER_SMTP_SENDER=authelia@aurora.local

# ---- Media package API keys ----
# Sonarr:    Settings -> General -> API Key
HOMEPAGE_VAR_SONARR_KEY=
# Radarr:    Settings -> General -> API Key
HOMEPAGE_VAR_RADARR_KEY=
# Prowlarr:  Settings -> General -> API Key
HOMEPAGE_VAR_PROWLARR_KEY=
# Bazarr:    Settings -> General -> API Key
HOMEPAGE_VAR_BAZARR_KEY=

# RDTClient local admin (set on first visit to http://rdtclient.aurora.local)
HOMEPAGE_VAR_RDT_USER=
HOMEPAGE_VAR_RDT_PASS=

# qBittorrent (behind gluetun)
HOMEPAGE_VAR_QBIT_USER=admin
HOMEPAGE_VAR_QBIT_PASS=

# ---- Privacy package ----
# AdGuard: Settings -> General -> HTTP Basic Auth (created on setup wizard)
HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_USER=
HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_PASS=
apps.caddy_snippet:
# aurora.local / packages/core / caddy.snippet
#
# Phase D — Aurora manages the SSO surface. Two things live in this file:
#
#   1. The auth.{$DOMAIN} vhost — Authelia's own UI (login screen,
#      TOTP + WebAuthn enrolment, password reset).
#
#   2. The reusable (authelia) named route — any package whose
#      manifest.yml declares `sso.protect: true` gets an
#      `import authelia` injected into its vhost block by
#      Aurora's CaddySnippetService (D6). The line hands the request
#      through Authelia's forward-auth endpoint before the reverse
#      proxy fires.
#
# You no longer hand-edit per-package caddy.snippet files to opt into
# SSO — the sso: block in each manifest is the source of truth, and
# Aurora writes data/caddy/snippets/<pkg>.caddy with the import line
# injected. See packages/dashboard/backend/…/CaddySnippetService.java.
#
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Group cascade (Aurora role → Authelia groups) — reproduced from
# AutheliaService.groupsFor(). Used by Authelia's access_control rules
# (configuration.yml) to gate access by role:
#
#   ADMIN  → [admins, users, guests]
#   USER   → [users, guests]
#   GUEST  → [guests]
#
# So an access-control rule with `subject: 'group:users'` covers
# authenticated USER + ADMIN, and `subject: 'group:admins'` gates
# on ADMIN only.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---- Reusable forward-auth snippet ---------------------------------
# Every protected vhost imports this. Order of directives matters:
#
#   1. Strip any client-supplied Remote-* / X-Authelia-* headers on
#      the incoming request. Without this, a malicious LAN device
#      could set `Remote-User: admin` and impersonate the admin —
#      the upstream service would trust the header because the
#      request came from Caddy (10.x aurora_net bridge address).
#
#   2. Ask Authelia whether the request is allowed. On allow,
#      Authelia's 200 response carries Remote-User / Remote-Groups /
#      Remote-Email / Remote-Name — copy_headers merges them into
#      the request Caddy passes upstream.
#
#   3. Downstream reverse_proxy directives in the vhost see a
#      request with trustworthy Remote-* headers set. Services that
#      support trusted-header auth (Grafana, Paperless) can key
#      their session on Remote-User.
(authelia) {
	# 1. Strip any client-supplied trusted-header candidates.
	request_header -Remote-User
	request_header -Remote-Groups
	request_header -Remote-Email
	request_header -Remote-Name

	# 2. Ask Authelia. copy_headers merges Remote-* from the response
	# into the request Caddy passes upstream on success.
	forward_auth authelia:9091 {
		uri /api/authz/forward-auth
		copy_headers Remote-User Remote-Groups Remote-Email Remote-Name

		# X-Forwarded-* headers tell Authelia what the original
		# request looked like. Caddy sets these by default, but pin
		# them here so a future Caddy config change (e.g. header
		# stripping in the apex) doesn't silently break the
		# forward-auth handshake.
		header_up X-Forwarded-Method {method}
		header_up X-Forwarded-Proto {scheme}
		header_up X-Forwarded-Host {host}
		header_up X-Forwarded-Uri {uri}
		header_up X-Forwarded-For {remote_host}
	}
}

# ---- Authelia's own portal (auth.{$DOMAIN}) ------------------------
# The login / 2FA-enrolment / password-reset UI. MUST NOT import
# `authelia` itself — Authelia access_control has an explicit bypass
# for this vhost (configuration.yml). Circular auth would loop the
# browser forever.
#
# Also: `import no_hsts` scrubs any HSTS header the upstream sets,
# matching the apex + LAN-IP vhost policy in packages/core/caddy/
# Caddyfile. Some browsers with a stale HSTS from a previous
# home.local install would otherwise be locked into https-only when
# Bruce first hits http://auth.aurora.local/.
http://auth.{$DOMAIN} {
	import no_hsts
	reverse_proxy authelia:9091
}
https://auth.{$DOMAIN} {
	tls internal
	import no_hsts
	reverse_proxy authelia:9091
}

# ---- Stalwart admin UI + JMAP (mail-admin.{$DOMAIN}) ----------------
# Stalwart's HTTP surface: the setup wizard, admin console and JMAP,
# served on :8080 inside aurora_net (never host-published, so it never
# fights Caddy for :443).
#
# Gated with a hand-written `import authelia`. core has NO sso: block on
# purpose — an sso: block would gate every core vhost including the apex
# dashboard and could lock the operator out of the control plane, so the
# admin UI opts in here per-vhost instead. CaddySnippetService copies
# authored snippets through verbatim, so this import survives regen.
#
# Admin-only is enforced by an access_control rule for this exact host in
# packages/core/authelia/configuration.yml (subject group:admins), not by
# this file — `import authelia` only requires *an* authenticated session.
http://mail-admin.{$DOMAIN} {
	import authelia
	reverse_proxy stalwart:8080
}
https://mail-admin.{$DOMAIN} {
	tls internal
	import authelia
	reverse_proxy stalwart:8080
}
apps.readme:
# core

Always-on: Caddy, the reverse proxy and local HTTPS terminator.

Every other package's vhost is served under `*.$DOMAIN`. The apex
`$DOMAIN` itself reverse-proxies to `packages/dashboard` (Aurora) —
Aurora is the dashboard; there is no separate tile-grid app to run
alongside it.

## First-run

1. Set `DOMAIN` in `.env` (default `aurora.local`).
2. `./scripts/up.sh core`
3. Install Caddy's root CA on client devices for HTTPS:
   `./scripts/get-caddy-root-cert.sh`

apps.title: Dev sandbox (code-server + Postgres + Redis)
apps.description:
Browser-based VS Code (code-server) plus a Postgres 16 and Redis 7
instance for general dev/prototyping. code-server has ~/aurora.local
bind-mounted at /workspace/aurora.local so you can edit this repo from
any browser. Postgres/Redis are reachable from other packages on
aurora_net at postgres:5432 and redis:6379.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/dev
#
# General dev sandbox: code-server (VS Code in browser) plus a Postgres
# 16 and Redis 7 you can point apps at.
#
# Other packages on aurora_net reach these via container name:
#   postgres:5432
#   redis:6379
# Host-side ports are remapped (15432 / 16379) so they don't collide with
# a locally-installed pg/redis.

name: aurora-dev

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  code-server:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/code-server:latest
    container_name: code-server
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - PUID=${PUID:-1000}
      - PGID=${PGID:-1000}
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - PASSWORD=${CODE_SERVER_PASSWORD}
      - SUDO_PASSWORD=${CODE_SERVER_SUDO_PASSWORD:-}
      - DEFAULT_WORKSPACE=/workspace/aurora.local
    volumes:
      - ../../data/dev/code-server:/config
      # Edit this repo from the browser. UID 1000:1000 by default; if
      # your host user differs, override PUID/PGID in .env.
      - /home/${HOME_USER:-bruce}/aurora.local:/workspace/aurora.local:rw
    ports:
      - "8443:8443"

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - POSTGRES_USER=${POSTGRES_USER}
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=${POSTGRES_DB}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/dev/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "15432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    command:
      - redis-server
      - --requirepass
      - ${REDIS_PASSWORD}
      - --appendonly
      - "yes"
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/dev/redis:/data
    ports:
      - "16379:6379"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "-a", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/dev / .env.example
#
# Copy to .env and fill in.

TZ=Europe/London

# UID/GID for code-server. Defaults match group_vars/all.yml home_uid/gid.
# PUID=1000
# PGID=1000
# HOME_USER=bruce  # used for the /home/${HOME_USER}/aurora.local bind mount

# ---- code-server ----
# Web UI login. Anything you want, but pick something long.
CODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=
# Optional. If set, `sudo` inside the code-server terminal will prompt
# for this. Leave blank to disable sudo.
CODE_SERVER_SUDO_PASSWORD=

# ---- Postgres ----
POSTGRES_USER=dev
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=
POSTGRES_DB=dev

# ---- Redis ----
REDIS_PASSWORD=
apps.readme:
# dev

Browser-based **VS Code (code-server)** plus **Postgres 16** and
**Redis 7** for general dev work / prototyping.

## First-run

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`. Set `CODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`,
   `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `REDIS_PASSWORD`.
2. `./scripts/up.sh core dev`
3. Access:
   - code-server: `https://code.$DOMAIN/`
   - Postgres (from host): `psql -h localhost -p 15432 -U $POSTGRES_USER $POSTGRES_DB`
   - Redis (from host): `redis-cli -h localhost -p 16379 -a $REDIS_PASSWORD`

## Editing this repo from the browser

`~/aurora.local` is bind-mounted into code-server at
`/workspace/aurora.local`. Open that folder and you can edit the entire
repo from anywhere on the LAN.

**UID caveat.** code-server runs as UID 1000 by default (via
`PUID=1000` / `PGID=1000`). If your host user is *not* 1000, override
`PUID` and `PGID` in `.env` before first-up, or files created in the
container will be owned by the wrong host user.

## Connecting other packages to Postgres/Redis

Both are on `aurora_net`, so any other package's container can reach:

- `postgres:5432` — internal Postgres port (not the remapped 15432)
- `redis:6379`   — internal Redis port (not 16379)

Example compose snippet in another package:

```yaml
environment:
  - DATABASE_URL=postgres://dev:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/dev
  - REDIS_URL=redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379/0
```

## Ports

Host ports are remapped so they don't collide with locally-installed
Postgres / Redis. See `manifest.yml`.

apps.title: Documents (Paperless-ngx + Stirling-PDF)
apps.description:
Paperless-ngx is a document management system: OCRs paper scans,
tags them, and gives you a searchable archive. Gotenberg + Apache
Tika are its office-file and content-extraction sidecars.
Stirling-PDF is an unrelated but complementary browser-based PDF
toolkit (split, merge, sign, redact, etc.).
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/documents
#
# Paperless-ngx (document DMS + OCR) with its Gotenberg / Tika
# sidecars, backed by a dedicated Postgres + Redis. Plus Stirling-PDF
# as a general-purpose browser PDF toolkit.
#
# The Postgres/Redis instances here are *scoped* to Paperless — they
# stay on aurora_net but no other package should touch them.

name: aurora-documents

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  paperless:
    image: ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:latest
    container_name: paperless
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    depends_on:
      paperless-postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      paperless-redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      paperless-gotenberg:
        condition: service_started
      paperless-tika:
        condition: service_started
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - USERMAP_UID=1000
      - USERMAP_GID=1000
      - PAPERLESS_TIME_ZONE=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE=${PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE:-eng}
      - PAPERLESS_REDIS=redis://paperless-redis:6379
      - PAPERLESS_DBHOST=paperless-postgres
      - PAPERLESS_DBUSER=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBPASS=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_DBNAME=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_TIKA_ENABLED=1
      - PAPERLESS_TIKA_ENDPOINT=http://paperless-tika:9998
      - PAPERLESS_TIKA_GOTENBERG_ENDPOINT=http://paperless-gotenberg:3000
      - PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY}
      - PAPERLESS_URL=${PAPERLESS_URL:-}
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER}
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      # ---- Phase D SSO (D12) -------------------------------------------
      # Trust the Remote-User header Caddy attaches on Authelia's
      # behalf. Paperless auto-provisions a matching account on first
      # visit; the seeded PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER stays as the emergency-
      # access super-user when Authelia is down.
      #
      # HTTP_REMOTE_USER is the WSGI-mangled name of the Remote-User
      # request header (gunicorn prefixes HTTP_ to every request header
      # per PEP 3333). Paperless-ngx documentation calls this out
      # explicitly — do not change to Remote-User here.
      #
      # Safe when SSO is disabled: no header → no auto-login →
      # Paperless's own login page renders as usual.
      - PAPERLESS_ENABLE_HTTP_REMOTE_USER=true
      - PAPERLESS_HTTP_REMOTE_USER_HEADER_NAME=HTTP_REMOTE_USER
      - PAPERLESS_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL=https://auth.${DOMAIN:-aurora.local}/logout
    volumes:
      - ../../data/documents/paperless/data:/usr/src/paperless/data
      - ../../data/documents/paperless/media:/usr/src/paperless/media
      - ../../data/documents/paperless/export:/usr/src/paperless/export
      - ../../data/documents/paperless/consume:/usr/src/paperless/consume
    ports:
      - "8010:8000"

  paperless-postgres:
    image: docker.io/library/postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: paperless-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - POSTGRES_USER=paperless
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=paperless
    volumes:
      - ../../data/documents/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U paperless -d paperless"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  paperless-redis:
    image: docker.io/library/redis:7-alpine
    container_name: paperless-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    volumes:
      - ../../data/documents/redis:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  paperless-gotenberg:
    image: docker.io/gotenberg/gotenberg:8
    container_name: paperless-gotenberg
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    # Paperless calls into gotenberg for office-file rendering. The
    # default chromium sandbox needs these flags in a container.
    command:
      - "gotenberg"
      - "--chromium-disable-javascript=true"
      - "--chromium-allow-list=file:///tmp/.*"

  paperless-tika:
    image: docker.io/apache/tika:latest
    container_name: paperless-tika
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]

  # ---- Stirling-PDF: general browser PDF toolkit -----------------------
  stirling-pdf:
    image: docker.io/frooodle/s-pdf:latest
    container_name: stirling-pdf
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY=false
    volumes:
      - ../../data/documents/stirling/config:/configs
      - ../../data/documents/stirling/logs:/logs
      - ../../data/documents/stirling/tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata
    ports:
      - "8020:8080"
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/documents / .env
#
# Copy to .env and fill in.
#   cp .env.example .env

TZ=Europe/London

# ---- Paperless-ngx admin ----
# Only used to seed the initial superuser on first boot; changes here
# after first run are ignored (Paperless stores users in the DB).
PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=admin
PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=

# ---- Paperless secret key (CRITICAL) ----
# Signs session cookies and password-reset tokens. If this leaks,
# anyone can forge sessions. Generate:
#   openssl rand -base64 48
# Rotating it invalidates every logged-in session; it does NOT
# invalidate stored documents.
PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=

# ---- Paperless external URL ----
# Set this to the canonical URL you'll access Paperless on, so it can
# build correct absolute links (feeds, email, etc.). Example:
#   PAPERLESS_URL=https://paperless.aurora.local
PAPERLESS_URL=

# ---- Paperless database ----
# Postgres superuser password for the paperless-postgres sidecar.
#   openssl rand -hex 24
PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD=

# ---- OCR ----
# Space-separated Tesseract language codes to install/use. Common:
#   eng deu fra spa nld ita
PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE=eng
apps.readme:
# documents (Paperless-ngx + Stirling-PDF)

Two complementary tools:

- **Paperless-ngx** — a searchable, tagged, OCR'd archive of every
  paper document that ever came into your house. Gotenberg handles
  office-file → PDF conversion; Tika extracts text from formats
  Tesseract can't.
- **Stirling-PDF** — a browser-based PDF Swiss army knife (split,
  merge, sign, redact, watermark, OCR, compress).

## Auth

Paperless honors `Remote-User` when Aurora manages SSO (see `sso:`
in `manifest.yml`). Signing into Aurora auto-provisions a matching
Paperless account on first visit — no second login page. The
seeded `PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER` stays as the emergency-access
superuser when Authelia is down.

Stirling-PDF has no user model of its own; it gets edge-gated by
Authelia when SSO is on and is otherwise open on the LAN.

When SSO is disabled, sign into Paperless with the seeded admin
from `.env` — same behaviour as before Aurora managed identity.
## First-run

1. `cp .env.example .env` and fill in:
   ```
   openssl rand -base64 48   # PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY
   openssl rand -hex 24      # PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD
   ```
   Set `PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER` / `PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`.

2. `./scripts/up.sh core documents`

3. Paperless: `https://paperless.$DOMAIN/` (or `http://<host>:8010`)
4. Stirling: `https://pdf.$DOMAIN/`     (or `http://<host>:8020`)

## Consumption folder

Drop PDFs / images into `data/documents/paperless/consume/` and
Paperless will OCR + ingest automatically. Handy targets:

- Samba share (see `packages/storage`) pointed at the consume dir.
- Scanner "Scan to Folder" over SMB.
- `rclone` mount from a cloud drive.

## OCR languages

Set `PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE` in `.env` to a space-separated list of
Tesseract language codes (e.g. `eng deu`). The default `eng` covers
US/UK English.

## Security notes

- **`PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY` is a real secret**, not decoration. Keep it
  out of git (it already is via .env / .gitignore). Rotating it will
  log every user out but does not destroy documents.
- Stirling-PDF runs with `DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY=false` for a simple
  single-user setup. Front it with Authelia / Authentik (see
  `packages/identity`) if you expose it beyond LAN.

## Backups

Back up `data/documents/paperless/{data,media,export}` and
`data/documents/postgres`. Stirling-PDF is stateless — its config
directory is regenerable.

## Ports

- 8010 → Paperless-ngx
- 8020 → Stirling-PDF

(Everything else stays on `aurora_net`.)

apps.title: Files (FileBrowser)
apps.description:
A file manager in the browser for the shared storage pool: browse,
preview, rename, upload and download without reaching for Samba or
SSH. Useful for the "just let me look at that file from my phone"
case, which is the one thing a network share is bad at.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/filebrowser
#
# A browser-based file manager over the shared storage pool. Samba
# already covers proper file access from a desktop; this covers the case
# Samba is bad at — looking at one file from a phone, or from someone
# else's laptop, without mounting anything.
#
# It runs as the same uid/gid as the pool owner so files it creates are
# not root-owned, which is the usual way this kind of container makes a
# mess that has to be chown'd out later.

name: aurora-filebrowser

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  filebrowser:
    image: filebrowser/filebrowser:v2.31.2
    container_name: filebrowser
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    user: "${PUID:-1000}:${PGID:-1000}"
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - FB_BASEURL=/
    volumes:
      # What it serves. The mergerfs pool by default; point this
      # somewhere else if the box has no pool.
      - ${STORAGE_ROOT:-/mnt/storage}:/srv
      # Its own database and settings.
      - ../../data/filebrowser:/database
    ports:
      - "8085:80"
    mem_limit: 512m
    cpus: 1.0
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider",
             "http://localhost:80/health"]
      start_period: 10s
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
apps.caddy_snippet:
# aurora.local / packages/filebrowser / caddy vhost fragment
#
# Fronts FileBrowser on files.${DOMAIN}. Behind Authelia, unlike most
# packages that carry their own accounts: this one can read and write
# every file in the pool, so it gets the same front door as the
# dashboard rather than relying on its own login.

http://files.{$DOMAIN} {
	import authelia
	reverse_proxy filebrowser:80
}
https://files.{$DOMAIN} {
	tls internal
	import authelia
	reverse_proxy filebrowser:80
}
apps.readme:
# Files (FileBrowser)

A file manager that runs in the browser, over the shared storage pool.

## Why this exists

Samba (the `storage` package) is the right tool for real file access: it
mounts as a drive, it is fast, and every desktop understands it. It is
bad at exactly one thing, which is looking at a single file from a device
you have not set up — a phone, a work laptop, someone else's machine.
CasaOS ships a file manager for this reason and it is the one feature of
theirs worth copying.

## What it can reach

Everything under `/mnt/storage`, read and write. That includes other
apps' data directories if they live in the pool.

This is why the vhost is behind Authelia rather than relying on
FileBrowser's own login: anyone who can sign in to Aurora can move or
delete anything it can see, so it should be no easier to reach than the
dashboard itself.

Its own database (users, shares, settings) lives under
`data/filebrowser` and is what the `backup:` block protects. The files it
manages belong to the pool and are covered by the pool's own backup.

## First run

1. `https://files.<your-domain>/`, signing in through Authelia first.
2. FileBrowser's own default account is `admin` / `admin`. Change it
   straight away under Settings → User Management. It is behind Authelia,
   so this is a second lock rather than the only one, but leaving a
   default password anywhere is how these things go wrong.
3. If the box has no mergerfs pool, edit the `/srv` bind mount in
   `compose.yml` to point at whatever you do want browsable.

## Not included

Sharing links to the outside world. FileBrowser supports them; Aurora
does not encourage them, because a public link out of the storage pool
bypasses every other control on the box. If you want that, turn it on
knowing what it does.

apps.title: Home automation (Home Assistant + MQTT + Zigbee2MQTT)
apps.description:
Home Assistant for automations, Mosquitto as the MQTT broker, and
Zigbee2MQTT (opt-in via 'zigbee' profile) to bridge a Zigbee USB
coordinator (CC2531, Sonoff ZBDongle-P/E, etc.) onto MQTT.

Home Assistant runs with network_mode: host — this is standard
practice and required for many local-discovery integrations (mDNS,
SSDP, HomeKit, Chromecast). It is therefore NOT attached to aurora_net.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/home-automation
#
# - Home Assistant runs with network_mode: host. This is intentional
#   and matches HA's own recommendation: many integrations rely on
#   L2 discovery (mDNS/SSDP/HomeKit) that a bridge network breaks.
#   Consequence: HA is NOT on aurora_net; Caddy reverse-proxies it via
#   host.docker.internal:8123 (or the host's LAN IP).
#
# - Mosquitto and Zigbee2MQTT sit on aurora_net. HA reaches Mosquitto
#   over the host's LAN IP (or 127.0.0.1) on 1883 since it's on
#   host networking.
#
# - Zigbee2MQTT is opt-in via COMPOSE_PROFILES=zigbee so users without
#   a coordinator don't get device-not-found errors.

name: aurora-automation

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  homeassistant:
    image: ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:stable
    container_name: homeassistant
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/home-automation/homeassistant:/config
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
      - /run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro

  mosquitto:
    image: eclipse-mosquitto:2
    container_name: mosquitto
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    ports:
      - "1883:1883"
      - "8883:8883"
    volumes:
      - ../../data/home-automation/mosquitto/config:/mosquitto/config
      - ../../data/home-automation/mosquitto/data:/mosquitto/data
      - ../../data/home-automation/mosquitto/log:/mosquitto/log

  zigbee2mqtt:
    image: koenkk/zigbee2mqtt:latest
    container_name: zigbee2mqtt
    restart: unless-stopped
    profiles: ["zigbee"]
    networks: [aurora_net]
    depends_on:
      - mosquitto
    ports:
      # Zigbee2MQTT frontend listens on 8080 internally; remap to 8084
      # on the host to avoid colliding with gluetun's 8080 publish.
      - "8084:8080"
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
    # Passthrough of the Zigbee coordinator. Default to /dev/ttyUSB0
    # but expect users to override with a stable by-id path.
    devices:
      - ${ZIGBEE_ADAPTER:-/dev/ttyUSB0}:/dev/ttyACM0
    volumes:
      - ../../data/home-automation/zigbee2mqtt:/app/data
      - /run/udev:/run/udev:ro
apps.env_example:
# Copy to .env and edit.
# Every KEY referenced by compose.yml is listed here.

TZ=Europe/London

# ---- Zigbee coordinator (profile: zigbee) --------------------------
# Path to your Zigbee USB stick. Prefer a stable /dev/serial/by-id/
# path so a reboot / re-plug can't renumber it.
#
# Examples:
#   Sonoff ZBDongle-P (CP2102):
#     ZIGBEE_ADAPTER=/dev/serial/by-id/usb-ITead_Sonoff_Zigbee_3.0_USB_Dongle_Plus_XXXXXXXX-if00-port0
#   Sonoff ZBDongle-E (CH9102):
#     ZIGBEE_ADAPTER=/dev/serial/by-id/usb-1a86_USB_Single_Serial_XXXXXXXX-if00
#   ConBee II:
#     ZIGBEE_ADAPTER=/dev/serial/by-id/usb-dresden_elektronik_ConBee_II_DE2XXXXXX-if00
#   CC2531 (legacy):
#     ZIGBEE_ADAPTER=/dev/ttyACM0
#
# If unset, defaults to /dev/ttyUSB0 (may not exist — profile off is safer).
ZIGBEE_ADAPTER=/dev/ttyUSB0
apps.readme:
# home-automation

Home Assistant + Mosquitto (MQTT) + Zigbee2MQTT.

## Auth

Home Assistant keeps its own username/password flow and 2FA setup
because HA's trusted-header integration is fiddly (needs
`trusted_networks` provider tweaks + IP whitelisting that fights
Caddy's aurora_net container IP). Aurora's manifest declares
`sso.trusted_headers: false` for this package.

With SSO on, Authelia gates `https://ha.$DOMAIN/` at the edge — no
unauthenticated LAN device can reach HA's login page, but once
you're through Authelia you still type your HA credentials.
Second factor lives inside HA.

Zigbee2MQTT has no auth at all, so Authelia is its only wall.

With SSO off, everything is as before Phase D: HA login on
`ha.$DOMAIN`, no gate.

## Host networking caveat

Home Assistant runs with `network_mode: host`. This is HA's own
recommendation: local-discovery integrations (Chromecast, HomeKit,
mDNS, SSDP) do not survive a docker bridge network. Consequence:

- HA is **not** attached to `aurora_net`.
- Caddy in `core` reaches it via `host.docker.internal:8123` (Linux
  has `extra_hosts: host-gateway` on the caddy service).
- HA reaches Mosquitto over the host's LAN IP or 127.0.0.1:1883 (not
  by container name).

Mosquitto and Zigbee2MQTT stay on `aurora_net` and are reachable by
name from other packages.

## First-run

1. `./scripts/up.sh core home-automation`
2. Complete HA onboarding at `http://<lan-ip>:8123`.
3. In HA: Settings → Devices & Services → Add MQTT integration.
   Point at `<lan-ip>:1883`.

## Mosquitto credentials

The broker starts anonymous by default (dev-friendly). Before
exposing it, create a user and lock it down:

    docker exec -it mosquitto \
        mosquitto_passwd -c /mosquitto/config/passwd myuser

Then edit `data/home-automation/mosquitto/config/mosquitto.conf`:

    allow_anonymous false
    password_file /mosquitto/config/passwd
    listener 1883
    listener 8883
    # ...cafile/certfile/keyfile for TLS if desired

Restart mosquitto: `docker restart mosquitto`.

## Zigbee2MQTT (profile: `zigbee`)

Zigbee2MQTT is opt-in — enable only if you have a Zigbee coordinator.

1. Plug in the USB coordinator (Sonoff ZBDongle-P/E, ConBee II,
   CC2531, etc.).
2. Find its stable path:
       ls -l /dev/serial/by-id/
3. Set `ZIGBEE_ADAPTER` in `.env` to that path.
4. Create `data/home-automation/zigbee2mqtt/configuration.yaml` with
   the minimum:

        homeassistant: true
        permit_join: false
        mqtt:
          base_topic: zigbee2mqtt
          server: mqtt://mosquitto:1883
        serial:
          port: /dev/ttyACM0
        frontend:
          port: 8080

5. Bring up with the profile:

        COMPOSE_PROFILES=zigbee ./scripts/up.sh core home-automation
        # or, if scripts/up.sh gains a --zigbee flag:
        ./scripts/up.sh --zigbee core home-automation

6. Web UI: `http://<lan-ip>:8084` (remapped from 8080 to avoid
   colliding with gluetun's qBittorrent publish).

## Ports

See `manifest.yml`.

apps.title: Media server (Jellyfin)
apps.description:
Jellyfin is a free, self-hosted media server: it plays the films, TV,
and music the arr stack collects, to a browser, a TV app, or a phone.
No account, no subscription, hardware transcoding included. Seerr
(in the media package) points at it for requests.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/jellyfin
#
# The media *server* the arr stack was missing. Sonarr/Radarr acquire;
# Jellyfin plays. Seerr (in packages/media) points its "media server"
# setting at this. Free, no account, no paywalled transcoding.
#
# Fronted by Caddy on jellyfin.${DOMAIN}. Deliberately NOT behind
# Authelia: native TV/mobile clients don't speak forward-auth, so
# Jellyfin uses its own accounts. Libraries are mounted read-only —
# Jellyfin reads media, it never writes to it.

name: aurora-jellyfin

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  jellyfin:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/jellyfin:latest
    container_name: jellyfin
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      # Behind Caddy the base URL is the vhost. Set this so Jellyfin's
      # own "remote access" links and clients report the right address.
      - JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl=${JELLYFIN_PUBLISHED_URL:-https://jellyfin.${DOMAIN:-aurora.local}}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/jellyfin:/config
      # Same library roots the arr stack writes into, read-only here.
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/tv:/data/tv:ro
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/movies:/data/movies:ro
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/music:/data/music:ro
    ports:
      # HTTP UI/API. Caddy proxies this; the port is published so the
      # first-run wizard is reachable before the vhost is wired.
      - "8096:8096"
      # Optional client auto-discovery on the LAN (uncomment if wanted):
      #   - "7359:7359/udp"   # Jellyfin client discovery
      #   - "1900:1900/udp"   # DLNA (conflicts with packages/storage minidlna)
    # ---- Hardware transcoding (opt-in) --------------------------------
    # Intel/AMD iGPU (VAAPI/QSV): uncomment and, in the Jellyfin
    # dashboard, set Playback > Transcoding to VAAPI or QSV with device
    # /dev/dri/renderD128. The reference box (i5-6500T) has Intel QuickSync.
    #   devices:
    #     - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    #   group_add:
    #     - "989"   # the host `render` group GID (getent group render)
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://localhost:8096/health"]
      start_period: 30s
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
apps.caddy_snippet:
# aurora.local / packages/jellyfin / caddy vhost fragment
#
# Fronts Jellyfin on jellyfin.${DOMAIN}. Wired into
# packages/core/caddy/Caddyfile by the installer's `import` mechanism.
#
# NOTE: no `import authelia` here, on purpose. Jellyfin's native TV and
# mobile clients cannot follow a forward-auth redirect, so Jellyfin owns
# its own accounts. Do not put it behind Authelia unless you only ever
# use the web UI.
#
# reverse_proxy handles Jellyfin's websockets automatically. The larger
# body limit keeps subtitle/artwork uploads from the admin UI happy.

http://jellyfin.{$DOMAIN} {
	reverse_proxy jellyfin:8096
}
https://jellyfin.{$DOMAIN} {
	tls internal
	request_body {
		max_size 100MB
	}
	reverse_proxy jellyfin:8096
}
apps.readme:
# jellyfin

The media server. Sonarr and Radarr fetch the files; Jellyfin plays
them, to a browser, a smart-TV app, or a phone. Free, no account, no
paywalled features.

This is the default `media-player` variant. If Plex or Emby packages are
added later, the picker offers them as alternatives to this one.

## First-run

1. `./scripts/up.sh jellyfin`
2. Open `https://jellyfin.$DOMAIN/` and complete the setup wizard.
   Jellyfin has its own accounts; it is **not** behind Authelia (native
   clients can't follow a forward-auth redirect).
3. Add libraries pointing at:
   - `/data/tv` — the arr stack's TV root
   - `/data/movies` — the arr stack's film root
   - `/data/music`
   These are the same folders under `$MEDIA_ROOT`, mounted read-only.
4. In **Seerr** (`packages/media`), set the media server to this
   Jellyfin so requests reconcile against what you already own.

## Hardware transcoding

Software transcoding is CPU-heavy. The reference box's Intel iGPU does
QuickSync. To use it:

1. In `compose.yml`, uncomment the `devices:` and `group_add:` block
   under the `jellyfin` service. Set the GID to the host `render` group
   (`getent group render`).
2. `./scripts/up.sh jellyfin`
3. Jellyfin dashboard > **Playback > Transcoding**: set VAAPI or QSV,
   device `/dev/dri/renderD128`.

## Why not behind Authelia?

Jellyfin's TV and mobile apps authenticate against Jellyfin directly and
cannot complete an Authelia login redirect. Fronting it with forward-auth
breaks those clients. The `caddy.snippet` therefore proxies it without
`import authelia`. Keep it that way unless you only use the web UI.

## Environment

No `.env` is required: every value has a working default. To override,
create `packages/jellyfin/.env` with any of:

```
TZ=Europe/London
DOMAIN=aurora.local
# Must match packages/media so Jellyfin sees the same library folders:
MEDIA_ROOT=/home/bruce/media
JELLYFIN_PUBLISHED_URL=https://jellyfin.aurora.local
# Homepage widget API key (Jellyfin > Dashboard > API Keys), optional:
JELLYFIN_KEY=
```

## Ports

See `manifest.yml`.

## Integration

- `caddy.snippet` fronts the UI on `jellyfin.$DOMAIN`.
- `homepage.yml` adds a Jellyfin tile with a now-playing widget (needs a
  `JELLYFIN_KEY` API key from Jellyfin > Dashboard > API Keys).

apps.title: Media automation (*arr + requests + downloaders)
apps.description:
Debrid-first (RDTClient) with qBittorrent-behind-gluetun as the local
fallback. Sonarr/Radarr/Bazarr/Prowlarr do the automation, Seerr
handles requests, Flaresolverr rides shotgun on Cloudflare challenges.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/media
#
# Opinionated: Debrid-first (RDTClient) with qBittorrent behind gluetun
# as the local fallback. Sonarr/Radarr/Bazarr/Prowlarr do the automation,
# Seerr does requests, Flaresolverr rides shotgun on the cloudflare
# challenges Prowlarr occasionally hits.
#
# qBittorrent uses `network_mode: "service:gluetun"` so it *must* be
# brought up as part of `docker compose -f privacy -f media up -d`
# (which scripts/up.sh handles).

name: aurora-media

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

x-arr-common: &arr-common
  restart: unless-stopped
  networks: [aurora_net]
  environment:
    - PUID=1000
    - PGID=1000
    - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}

services:
  sonarr:
    <<: *arr-common
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/sonarr:latest
    container_name: sonarr
    volumes:
      - ../../data/sonarr:/config
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/tv:/tv
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/downloads:/downloads

  radarr:
    <<: *arr-common
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/radarr:latest
    container_name: radarr
    volumes:
      - ../../data/radarr:/config
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/movies:/movies
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/downloads:/downloads

  prowlarr:
    <<: *arr-common
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/prowlarr:latest
    container_name: prowlarr
    volumes:
      - ../../data/prowlarr:/config

  bazarr:
    <<: *arr-common
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/bazarr:latest
    container_name: bazarr
    volumes:
      - ../../data/bazarr:/config
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/tv:/tv
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/movies:/movies

  seerr:
    # Seerr (fork/successor of Jellyseerr, actively maintained).
    # https://docs.seerr.dev/getting-started/docker/
    # Runs as the built-in `node` user (UID 1000); doesn't use PUID/PGID.
    # iter-3 fix: image entrypoint runs as `node` and mkdir /app/config/logs
    # fails with EACCES when the host bind-mount is owned by anything other
    # than UID 1000 (e.g. root, or a different bruce UID). We override the
    # entrypoint to (a) start as root, (b) chown the mount to node:node,
    # (c) drop to node and exec the real entrypoint. `user: root` is only
    # for the wrapper shell — su-exec / gosu-equivalent in the wrapper.
    image: ghcr.io/seerr-team/seerr:latest
    container_name: seerr
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    user: "0:0"
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
      - PORT=5055
    volumes:
      - ../../data/seerr:/app/config
    entrypoint:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -e
        mkdir -p /app/config/logs
        chown -R node:node /app/config
        exec su node -s /bin/sh -c 'docker-entrypoint.sh npm start'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider",
             "http://localhost:5055/api/v1/settings/public"]
      start_period: 20s
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3

  flaresolverr:
    <<: *arr-common
    image: ghcr.io/flaresolverr/flaresolverr:latest
    container_name: flaresolverr
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - LOG_LEVEL=info

  rdtclient:
    <<: *arr-common
    image: rogerfar/rdtclient:latest
    container_name: rdtclient
    volumes:
      - ../../data/rdtclient/data:/data/db
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/downloads:/data/downloads

  # ---- qBittorrent, VPN-tunnelled ----
  # Opt-in via COMPOSE_PROFILES=torrent. Shares gluetun's netns so all
  # traffic (peer + tracker) egresses through the VPN. gluetun's
  # kill-switch means if the tunnel drops qbit gets no network.
  qbittorrent:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/qbittorrent:latest
    container_name: qbittorrent
    restart: unless-stopped
    profiles: ["torrent"]
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - WEBUI_PORT=8080
    volumes:
      - ../../data/qbittorrent:/config
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT:-/home/bruce/media}/downloads:/downloads
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/media / .env
#
# Everything here is optional — the arrs work without any of it, this
# is just for one-off overrides. All the API keys live in

apps.title: Monitoring (Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime-Kuma)
apps.description:
Prometheus scrapes node_exporter (host) and cAdvisor (containers),
Grafana visualises with an auto-provisioned Prometheus datasource,
and Uptime-Kuma provides blackbox HTTP health checks. Comes with a
ready-to-go dashboards folder — drop JSON dashboards into
grafana/provisioning/dashboards/ and they load on start.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/monitoring
#
# Observability trio for the aurora box:
#   - Prometheus scrapes node_exporter (host) and cAdvisor (containers),
#     plus anything else you wire in under prometheus/prometheus.yml.
#   - Grafana visualises. Datasource + dashboards folder are
#     auto-provisioned from grafana/provisioning/ so a fresh volume
#     comes up already pointed at Prometheus.
#   - Uptime-Kuma is a separate, self-contained blackbox monitor for
#     "is the URL up" style checks.
#
# All services join aurora_net so Caddy can front them on subdomains.

name: aurora-monitoring

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

x-common: &common
  restart: unless-stopped
  networks: [aurora_net]
  environment:
    - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}

services:
  prometheus:
    <<: *common
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    container_name: prometheus
    user: "${PUID:-1000}:${PUID:-1000}"
    command:
      - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - --storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus
      - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d
      - --web.enable-lifecycle
    volumes:
      - ../monitoring/prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ../../data/monitoring/prometheus:/prometheus
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"

  grafana:
    <<: *common
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    container_name: grafana
    user: "${PUID:-1000}:${PUID:-1000}"
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_ANALYTICS_REPORTING_ENABLED=false
      - GF_ANALYTICS_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES=false
      # ---- Phase D SSO (D12) -------------------------------------------
      # Trust Caddy's Remote-User / Remote-Email / Remote-Name headers
      # so an Aurora sign-in propagates into Grafana without a second
      # login page. Auto-provisioning creates a Grafana user on first
      # visit; Editor role by default so a household member can view +
      # tweak dashboards without touching alerts.
      #
      # Whitelisted proxy: the `caddy` container hostname on aurora_net.
      # A request that hits Grafana directly (bypassing Caddy) doesn't
      # match the whitelist, so Grafana falls back to normal basic-auth
      # with GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER/PASSWORD. That's the emergency-access
      # path when Authelia is down.
      #
      # Safe when SSO is disabled: Caddy simply doesn't set Remote-User,
      # Grafana sees no header, falls back to its own login. No harmful
      # interaction.
      - GF_AUTH_PROXY_ENABLED=true
      - GF_AUTH_PROXY_HEADER_NAME=Remote-User
      - GF_AUTH_PROXY_HEADER_PROPERTY=username
      - GF_AUTH_PROXY_HEADERS=Email:Remote-Email Name:Remote-Name Groups:Remote-Groups
      - GF_AUTH_PROXY_AUTO_SIGN_UP=true
      - GF_AUTH_PROXY_WHITELIST=caddy
      # Phase D iter-14 (D13). When a Grafana user hits Sign Out, kick
      # them through Authelia's logout so the shared .{DOMAIN} session
      # cookie is cleared — otherwise the next visit auto-signs them
      # right back in via auth_proxy.
      - GF_AUTH_SIGNOUT_REDIRECT_URL=https://auth.${DOMAIN:-aurora.local}/logout
    volumes:
      - ../monitoring/grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ../../data/monitoring/grafana:/var/lib/grafana
    ports:
      - "3001:3000"
    depends_on:
      - prometheus

  node-exporter:
    <<: *common
    image: prom/node-exporter:latest
    container_name: node-exporter
    command:
      - --path.rootfs=/host
      - --collector.filesystem.mount-points-exclude=^/(sys|proc|dev|host|etc)($$|/)
    pid: host
    volumes:
      - /:/host:ro,rslave
    ports:
      - "9100:9100"

  cadvisor:
    <<: *common
    image: gcr.io/cadvisor/cadvisor:latest
    container_name: cadvisor
    # cAdvisor needs a laundry list of host paths to introspect
    # container cgroups. Read-only where possible.
    privileged: true
    devices:
      - /dev/kmsg
    volumes:
      - /:/rootfs:ro
      - /var/run:/var/run:ro
      - /sys:/sys:ro
      - /var/lib/docker:/var/lib/docker:ro
      - /dev/disk/:/dev/disk:ro
    ports:
      - "8082:8080"

  uptime-kuma:
    <<: *common
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    volumes:
      - ../../data/monitoring/uptime-kuma:/app/data
    ports:
      - "3002:3001"
apps.env_example:
# Copy to .env and fill in.
#
# Every KEY substituted in compose.yml is listed here. Blank values
# fall back to the compose-side defaults where present.

TZ=Europe/London

# ---- Grafana admin ----
# Initial admin user + password. Change GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD before
# first `up` — Grafana persists the hash and won't re-read this later.
GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER=admin
GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD=changeme
apps.readme:
# monitoring

Prometheus + Grafana + node_exporter + cAdvisor + Uptime-Kuma.

## Auth

Grafana honors `Remote-User` / `Remote-Email` / `Remote-Name` /
`Remote-Groups` headers when Aurora manages SSO (see `sso: protect`
in `manifest.yml`). Signing into Aurora auto-provisions a matching
Grafana account on first visit — no second login page.

When SSO is disabled, `GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER` + `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD`
remain the sign-in credentials. They also stay in place as the
emergency-access super-user when Authelia is down.

Prometheus + Uptime-Kuma get edge-gated by Authelia when SSO is on —
no auto-provisioning, just "authenticated Aurora user or nothing".

## First-run

1. `cp .env.example .env` and set `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD`.
2. `./scripts/up.sh monitoring`
3. Grafana at `https://grafana.$DOMAIN/` — the Prometheus
   datasource is auto-provisioned, so you can `+ Import` dashboard IDs
   straight away. Recommended starting kit:
   - **1860** — Node Exporter Full
   - **14282** — cAdvisor
   - **18283** — Kuma summary (if you export Kuma → Prom)
4. Uptime-Kuma at `https://uptime.$DOMAIN/` — set an admin
   password on the first-run wizard, then add monitors for each of
   your other services.

## Adding scrape targets

Edit `prometheus/prometheus.yml`. A few examples are commented in for
adguard, gluetun, caddy, uptime-kuma. Reload live with:

```
docker exec prometheus killall -HUP prometheus
```

## Persistent dashboards

Drop `*.json` (exported from Grafana) under
`grafana/provisioning/dashboards/`. Grafana rescans every 30s and
files there re-appear on a fresh volume.

## Ports

See `manifest.yml`.

## Integration

- `caddy.snippet` fronts grafana / prometheus / uptime on subdomains.
- `homepage.yml` fragment adds a "Monitoring" services group.
- Prometheus and cAdvisor URLs need no config beyond docker networking
  — everything scrapes over `aurora_net`.
