notes/PKM system with a live command palette, a plug ecosystem,
and an offline-capable PWA. Everything is a plain .md file on
disk, so your notes survive the tool.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/notes
#
# SilverBullet — single-user markdown notes with a plug system.
# Storage is just a directory full of .md files; no database.

name: aurora-notes

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  silverbullet:
    image: ghcr.io/silverbulletmd/silverbullet:latest
    container_name: silverbullet
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      # Built-in HTTP basic auth. SilverBullet reads user:password
      # from SB_USER / SB_PASSWORD env; falls back to open if unset.
      - SB_USER=${SB_USER}:${SB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/notes/silverbullet:/space
    # SilverBullet listens on 3000 internally; publish as 3030 to
    # avoid collision with AdGuard's :3000 first-run wizard.
    ports:
      - "3030:3000"
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/notes / .env
#
# Copy to .env and fill in.
#   cp .env.example .env

TZ=Europe/London

# ---- SilverBullet basic-auth ----
# SilverBullet has a single-user auth model.
#
# Two modes:
#
# 1) SSO enabled (recommended). Aurora manages Authelia forward-auth
#    on notes.$DOMAIN and BLANKS SB_USER + SB_PASSWORD here so
#    SilverBullet runs open internally — Authelia is the only wall.
#    Users sign into Aurora once and click through to Notes without
#    a second login.
#
#    Aurora blanks these values automatically when you tick the SSO
#    step in onboarding (or POST /api/onboarding/sso {enable:true}).
#    Leave them empty here if you're wiring SSO by hand.
#
# 2) SSO disabled (standalone). Fill in SB_USER + SB_PASSWORD below.
#    SilverBullet enforces HTTP basic auth internally; nobody
#    reaches the notes without knowing these credentials, but you
#    also don't get single-sign-on across the rest of the box.
SB_USER=admin
SB_PASSWORD=
apps.readme:
# notes (SilverBullet)

[SilverBullet](https://silverbullet.md/) is a hackable, markdown-native
personal knowledge system. Everything is a `.md` file in a folder
("space") — no database, no lock-in.

## First-run

### Option A — with Aurora SSO (recommended)

If you ticked "Single sign-on for services" in the Aurora onboarding
wizard, everything is already wired:

1. Aurora blanked `SB_USER` + `SB_PASSWORD` in `packages/notes/.env`
   so SilverBullet runs auth-less internally.
2. Caddy fronts `notes.$DOMAIN` with Authelia forward-auth.
3. `./scripts/up.sh core identity notes`
4. Sign into Aurora at `https://$DOMAIN/`. Click Notes. You land on
   SilverBullet without a second login.

Aurora's role model (admin / user / guest) gates access. The `notes`
package requires at least `user` (see `manifest.yml` → `sso.min_role`).

### Option B — standalone (no Aurora SSO)

1. `cp .env.example .env` and set `SB_USER` / `SB_PASSWORD` to a real
   value.
2. `./scripts/up.sh core notes`
3. Visit `https://notes.$DOMAIN/` and log in with those credentials.

SilverBullet's built-in single-user auth is the only wall in this mode.

## Storage

Notes live at `data/notes/silverbullet/`. Point `git init` at it and
commit — SilverBullet is happy to share the directory with git.
Alternatively rsync/restic it to your backup target.

## Mobile

There's no first-class native app. The web UI is a PWA:

- iOS Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen.
- Android Chrome → menu → Install app.

Both give you an offline-capable install with a splash screen.

## Ports

SilverBullet listens internally on 3000 but is published on **3030**
to avoid collision with AdGuard's :3000 first-run wizard.

## Extending

Plugs (extensions) are installed via the `PLUGS` page inside the app;
they're just URLs to `.plug.js` files. Ecosystem lives at
https://silverbullet.md/PLUGS.

apps.title: Photos (Immich)
apps.description:
Self-hosted photo & video backup with mobile apps, timeline, faces,
and search. Immich server + microservices + Postgres (pgvecto.rs) +
Redis + a machine-learning worker for CLIP / face detection.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/photos
#
# Immich: self-hosted photo/video backup with mobile apps.
#
# Stack:
#   - immich-server      : API + web UI (port 2283)
#   - immich-ml          : CLIP + face detection worker
#   - immich-redis       : queues
#   - immich-postgres    : pgvecto.rs (vector-search Postgres fork)
#
# Data lives under ../../data/photos/. UPLOAD_LOCATION in .env can
# override the library path to point at bulk storage.

name: aurora-photos

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  immich-server:
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    container_name: immich-server
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - DB_HOSTNAME=immich-postgres
      - DB_USERNAME=immich
      - DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - DB_DATABASE_NAME=immich
      - REDIS_HOSTNAME=immich-redis
      - JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET}
      - UPLOAD_LOCATION=${UPLOAD_LOCATION:-../../data/photos/library}
    volumes:
      - ${UPLOAD_LOCATION:-../../data/photos/library}:/usr/src/app/upload
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
    ports:
      - "2283:2283"
    depends_on:
      immich-redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      immich-postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "immich", "server-info"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 60s

  immich-ml:
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    container_name: immich-ml
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
    volumes:
      - ../../data/photos/ml-cache:/cache

  immich-redis:
    image: docker.io/redis:6.2-alpine
    container_name: immich-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  immich-postgres:
    image: docker.io/tensorchord/pgvecto-rs:pg14-v0.2.0
    container_name: immich-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - POSTGRES_USER=immich
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=immich
      - POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--data-checksums
    volumes:
      - ../../data/photos/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U immich -d immich"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

# aurora.local / packages/photos / .env
#
# Copy to .env in this directory and fill in.
#
#   cp .env.example .env
#
# See https://immich.app/docs/install/environment-variables

# ---- global ----
TZ=Europe/London

# ---- Immich release pin ----
# 'release' tracks the latest tagged release. Pin to e.g. v1.106.4 for
# reproducibility.
IMMICH_VERSION=release

# Where photo/video originals are stored. Defaults inside the repo

apps.readme:
# photos (Immich)

Self-hosted photo/video backup with real mobile apps, timeline view,
face recognition and CLIP-based semantic search.

## First-run

1. `cp .env.example .env`, then generate secrets:
   ```
   openssl rand -hex 32   # JWT_SECRET
   openssl rand -hex 24   # DB_PASSWORD
   ```
2. Optionally point `UPLOAD_LOCATION` at bulk storage (e.g.
   `/mnt/media/photos`) — the library grows fast.
3. `./scripts/up.sh core photos`
4. Visit `https://photos.$DOMAIN/` and register. **The first
   registered account is the admin.**
5. Install the Immich app on your phone (App Store / F-Droid / Play)
   and point it at the same URL to enable auto-backup.

## Mobile app

- iOS: https://apps.apple.com/app/immich/id1613945652
- Android (Play): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.alextran.immich
- Android (F-Droid): https://f-droid.org/packages/app.alextran.immich/

## Machine learning

`immich-ml` handles CLIP embeddings + face detection. The first pass
over an existing library can take hours on CPU; be patient. If you
have an NVIDIA GPU, swap the ML image for the CUDA variant (see
Immich docs).

## Backups

Two things to back up:

1. `../../data/photos/postgres` — the metadata database (small).
2. `$UPLOAD_LOCATION` — the actual originals (huge).

Only 2283 is exposed; the rest of the stack is on `aurora_net` only.

apps.title: Privacy (LAN DNS + VPN)
apps.description:
AdGuard Home is the LAN's DNS server + ad/tracker blocker; point
your router's DHCP DNS at this box after first boot. Gluetun is a
provider-agnostic VPN sidecar exposing its network namespace to
other packages (e.g. qBittorrent in media/torrent profile).
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/privacy
#
# - AdGuard Home is the LAN's DNS server + ad/tracker blocker.
#   Point your router's DHCP DNS at this box after first boot.
#   First-run wizard at http://<box-ip>:3000 sets admin creds;
#   afterwards the UI moves to https://adguard.aurora.local/.
#
# - Gluetun is a VPN sidecar. It exposes its network namespace to any
#   compose service that sets `network_mode: "service:gluetun"`.
#   Provider-agnostic: pick VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER in .env and fill in
#   the matching secret (wireguard key, openvpn creds, whatever).
#   qBittorrent in packages/media routes through it.

name: aurora-privacy

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  adguard:
    image: adguard/adguardhome:latest
    container_name: adguard
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    ports:
      # Binds every address by default so LAN clients reach DNS however
      # they find the box. That needs port 53 genuinely free: Debian's
      # systemd-resolved holds 127.0.0.53:53 until host/roles/dns-stub
      # turns its stub listener off. Set LAN_IP to a specific address
      # only if you are keeping that stub.
      - "${LAN_IP:-0.0.0.0}:53:53/tcp"
      - "${LAN_IP:-0.0.0.0}:53:53/udp"
      # First-boot setup wizard; can close after Caddy vhost works.
      - "3000:3000/tcp"
    volumes:
      - ../../data/adguard/work:/opt/adguardhome/work
      - ../../data/adguard/conf:/opt/adguardhome/conf

  gluetun:
    image: qmcgaw/gluetun:latest
    container_name: gluetun
    restart: unless-stopped
    # The reusable WireGuard egress gateway. Any app that sets
    # `network_mode: "service:gluetun"` egresses through the tunnel while
    # the host and every other container stay on the WAN. Started by the
    # `torrent` profile (for qBittorrent) or the `vpn` profile (to serve
    # any other app on its own). See docs/SPLIT_TUNNEL.md.
    profiles: ["torrent", "vpn"]
    networks: [aurora_net]
    cap_add: [NET_ADMIN]
    devices:
      - /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun
    # Explicit pass-through from the shell env (populated by scripts/up.sh
    # sourcing packages/privacy/.env). Docker compose env_file behaviour
    # with multi -f setups is unreliable, so we use pass-through instead.
    environment:
      - TZ
      - VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER
      - VPN_TYPE
      - WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY
      - WIREGUARD_ADDRESSES
      - WIREGUARD_PRESHARED_KEY
      - SERVER_COUNTRIES
      - SERVER_CITIES
      - OPENVPN_USER
      - OPENVPN_PASSWORD
      - FIREWALL
      - FIREWALL_INPUT_PORTS
      - FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS
      - FIREWALL_VPN_INPUT_PORTS
      - VPN_PORT_FORWARDING
      - VPN_PORT_FORWARDING_PROVIDER
      - PORT_FORWARD_ONLY
    ports:
      # qBittorrent web UI (packages/media/qbittorrent uses
      # network_mode: service:gluetun so its ports are published here).
      - "8080:8080"
      # gluetun control-server for the Homepage widget
      - "8000:8000"
    volumes:
      - ../../data/gluetun:/gluetun
    healthcheck:
      # Verifies the tunnel is actually passing traffic. Gluetun's own
      # /v1/* endpoints require auth by default; hitting an external
      # "what's my IP" service through the tunnel is a better signal.
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "--tries=1", "--timeout=5", "https://checkip.amazonaws.com"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/privacy / .env
#
# Copy to .env and fill in for your VPN provider.
# Gluetun docs: https://github.com/qdm12/gluetun-wiki

TZ=Europe/London

# LAN IP of this host — AdGuard binds :53 here so it doesn't fight
# with systemd-resolved on loopback. Set to your box's LAN address.
# 0.0.0.0 is the safe default: it binds every interface (works on any
# subnet) and is what compose.yml already falls back to when this is
# unset. A specific address only helps once it is genuinely your
# box's address, so this ships unset-equivalent rather than a guess.
LAN_IP=0.0.0.0

# ---- gluetun: provider selection --------------------------------------
# One of: protonvpn, mullvad, surfshark, nordvpn, airvpn, pia, ivpn,
# windscribe, ... (see gluetun-wiki for full list).
VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER=protonvpn
VPN_TYPE=wireguard

# ---- wireguard creds (VPN_TYPE=wireguard) -----------------------------
# ProtonVPN: https://account.protonvpn.com/downloads -> WireGuard config
#   Netshield:        No filter  (AdGuard already handles blocking)
#   VPN Accelerator:  On
#   Server type:      Standard   (not Secure Core)
#   Pick a server labelled BOTH P2P and PF (port-forwarding).
WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY=
WIREGUARD_ADDRESSES=10.2.0.2/32
# Optional: pin to a country/city.
SERVER_COUNTRIES=Netherlands
# SERVER_CITIES=

# ---- openvpn creds (VPN_TYPE=openvpn) ---------------------------------
# Only used if VPN_TYPE=openvpn. Leave blank for wireguard.
OPENVPN_USER=
OPENVPN_PASSWORD=

# ---- port forwarding (Proton, PIA, etc.) ------------------------------
# Enables NAT-PMP negotiation so qBittorrent gets a real listen port.
# Big deal for torrent connectivity. Set the qBittorrent listen port to
# match the forwarded port after first boot (Settings > Connection).
# On Proton the server MUST be labelled PF in the account portal.
VPN_PORT_FORWARDING=on
VPN_PORT_FORWARDING_PROVIDER=protonvpn

# ---- kill-switch is on by default. Leave these unless you know why. --
FIREWALL=on
FIREWALL_VPN_INPUT_PORTS=
FIREWALL_INPUT_PORTS=8080,8000
# Route your LAN so admin traffic isn't tunnelled.
FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS=192.168.0.0/24
apps.readme:
# privacy

- **AdGuard Home** — LAN DNS with ad/tracker blocking. Point your
  router's DHCP DNS at this box's IP after first boot.
- **Gluetun** — provider-agnostic VPN sidecar (opt-in via `torrent`
  profile). Other packages can share its netns with
  `network_mode: "service:gluetun"`.

## First-run

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`; pick a VPN provider and paste creds.
2. `./scripts/up.sh privacy`
3. Visit `http://<lan-ip>:3000` for AdGuard's setup wizard.
4. `./scripts/seed-adguard.sh` seeds the `*.aurora.local` DNS rewrites.
   Set the AdGuard admin account in the setup wizard (step 3).

apps.title: Roundcube (webmail)
apps.description:
Roundcube webmail for the box's mailboxes. A front end only — the mail
server (Stalwart) lives in the core stack; this connects to it over
IMAP/SMTP. The default webmail; SnappyMail is the lighter alternative
in the same group.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/roundcube
#
# Roundcube webmail — a front end only. The mail server (Stalwart) lives
# in packages/core; this connects to it over IMAP/SMTP on aurora_net.
# The default of the `webmail` variant group (SnappyMail is the lighter
# alternative).
#
# Bind-mount source paths resolve against packages/core/ (the first -f
# file), NOT this directory — see docs/PACKAGE_CONTRACT.md. Hence
# ../../data/roundcube/... rather than ./data.

name: aurora-roundcube

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  roundcube:
    image: roundcube/roundcubemail:latest
    container_name: roundcube
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      # sqlite keeps contacts/prefs without a second database container.
      - ROUNDCUBEMAIL_DB_TYPE=sqlite
      # Point at Stalwart in core. Stalwart requires TLS before it accepts
      # a PLAIN/LOGIN password, so use STARTTLS (tls://) on 143 / 587
      # rather than a bare plaintext connection. Stalwart's cert is
      # internal; if the handshake fails verification on first run see the
      # README for the one-line imap/smtp verify override.
      - ROUNDCUBEMAIL_DEFAULT_HOST=${WEBMAIL_IMAP_HOST:-tls://stalwart}
      - ROUNDCUBEMAIL_DEFAULT_PORT=${WEBMAIL_IMAP_PORT:-143}
      - ROUNDCUBEMAIL_SMTP_SERVER=${WEBMAIL_SMTP_HOST:-tls://stalwart}
      - ROUNDCUBEMAIL_SMTP_PORT=${WEBMAIL_SMTP_PORT:-587}
      - ROUNDCUBEMAIL_PLUGINS=archive,zipdownload,managesieve
      - ROUNDCUBEMAIL_UPLOAD_MAX_FILESIZE=25M
    volumes:
      - ../../data/roundcube/db:/var/roundcube/db
      - ../../data/roundcube/config:/var/roundcube/config
    # No host port on purpose. Roundcube serves on :80, reachable only via
    # Caddy at mail.$DOMAIN — which is gated by Authelia (see manifest
    # sso:). Publishing a host port here would let any LAN device reach the
    # webmail directly and walk straight around the Authelia gate.
apps.readme:
# roundcube (webmail)

[Roundcube](https://roundcube.net/) is the default webmail for the box.
It is a **front end only**: the mail server (Stalwart) lives in the core
stack, and Roundcube connects to it over IMAP/SMTP on the internal
`aurora_net`. It is the default of the `webmail` variant group; SnappyMail
(`packages/snappymail`) is the lighter alternative.

## First-run

1. **Create a mailbox on the mail server first.** Roundcube has no
   accounts of its own — it authenticates against Stalwart. Add one via
   the Stalwart admin UI at `https://mail-admin.$DOMAIN/` (or its API).
2. `cp packages/roundcube/.env.example packages/roundcube/.env` (optional;
   every value has a working default).
3. `./scripts/up.sh core roundcube`
4. Visit `https://mail.$DOMAIN/` and sign in with the full address and the
   mailbox password.

## Two logins, by design

`mail.$DOMAIN` is gated behind Authelia (`sso: protect: true`). Reaching
the inbox is two steps:

1. **Authelia** — sign in as an Aurora user (password + 2FA).
2. **Roundcube** — sign in to the mailbox with its IMAP password.

They are not redundant: Authelia authenticates *the person* (and hides the
webmail from any unauthenticated LAN device), while Roundcube needs the
actual mailbox password to open the IMAP session. True single-login would
need Stalwart to trust Authelia's tokens as its directory, which makes
Stalwart reject inbound mail to any address that hasn't logged in yet —
not a trade worth making for a mail server.

## Internal TLS to Stalwart

Stalwart will not accept a plaintext password, so Roundcube connects with
STARTTLS (`tls://stalwart` on 143 / 587). Stalwart's certificate is
internal, so on first run the handshake may fail peer verification. If so,
add a Roundcube config override to skip verification for that internal hop
(the browser-to-Caddy hop is still real HTTPS). Point the connection
elsewhere by setting `WEBMAIL_IMAP_HOST` / `WEBMAIL_SMTP_HOST` in
`packages/roundcube/.env`.

## Storage

`data/roundcube/` holds Roundcube's sqlite (contacts, preferences) and
config. The mail itself is Stalwart's, under `data/stalwart/`, and is
backed up by core. The manifest's `backup:` block keeps this address book
and settings so they survive a rebuild.

## Ports

None on the host. The webmail is reachable only via Caddy at `mail.$DOMAIN`,
behind Authelia — a published port would bypass that gate on the LAN. The
mail protocol ports (25/143/465/587/993) belong to Stalwart in core.

apps.title: SnappyMail (webmail)
apps.description:
SnappyMail is a light, fast webmail client — the lower-footprint
alternative to Roundcube in the `webmail` group. A front end only; it
connects to the mail server (Stalwart) in the core stack over IMAP.
Note it has shipped no tagged release since October 2024 (see the
README) — chosen deliberately for its weight, not its release cadence.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/snappymail
#
# SnappyMail webmail — the lighter alternative to Roundcube in the
# `webmail` variant group. Front end only; connects to the mail server
# (Stalwart, in packages/core) over IMAP on aurora_net.
#
# Bind-mount source paths resolve against packages/core/ (the first -f
# file) — see docs/PACKAGE_CONTRACT.md.

name: aurora-snappymail

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  snappymail:
    image: djmaze/snappymail:latest
    container_name: snappymail
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
    volumes:
      # Config, contacts and the admin password live here. IMAP servers
      # (Stalwart) are added through the admin panel on first run — see
      # the README; SnappyMail has no compose-level IMAP config.
      - ../../data/snappymail:/var/lib/snappymail
    # Serves on :8888. No host port on purpose — reachable only via Caddy
    # at snappymail.$DOMAIN, behind Authelia. A published port would walk
    # around that gate on the LAN.
apps.readme:
# snappymail (webmail)

[SnappyMail](https://snappymail.eu/) is a light, fast webmail client — the
lower-footprint alternative to Roundcube in the `webmail` variant group. It
is a **front end only**: the mail server (Stalwart) lives in the core
stack, and SnappyMail connects to it over IMAP on `aurora_net`.

## Maintenance warning (read this)

SnappyMail's last tagged release is **v2.38.2, October 2024**. The
repository is still committed to, but it has gone a long time without a
security release, and it has no SSO story. For a public-facing PHP app
that is a real risk. It is included because it is genuinely lighter and
nicer to use than Roundcube, but **Roundcube is the safer default** and
the recommended pick unless you specifically want the smaller footprint.

## First-run

1. **Create a mailbox on Stalwart** via its admin UI at
   `https://mail-admin.$DOMAIN/`.
2. `./scripts/up.sh core snappymail`
3. **Add the IMAP domain in SnappyMail's admin panel.** SnappyMail has no
   compose-level IMAP config; open `https://snappymail.$DOMAIN/?admin`. The
   admin password is written on first boot to
   `data/snappymail/_data_/_default_/admin_password.txt`. Add a domain
   pointing IMAP/SMTP at `stalwart` with STARTTLS (Stalwart requires TLS
   before it accepts a password).
4. Sign in at `https://snappymail.$DOMAIN/`.

## Two logins, by design

Same model as Roundcube: Authelia (password + 2FA) gates the front door,
then SnappyMail authenticates the mailbox over IMAP. Authelia proves the
person; SnappyMail needs the actual mailbox password to open the session.

## Storage

`data/snappymail/` holds config, contacts and the admin password. The mail
itself is Stalwart's, under `data/stalwart/`, backed up by core.

## Ports

None on the host. Reachable only via Caddy at `snappymail.$DOMAIN`, behind
Authelia. Its own vhost (not `mail.$DOMAIN`) so it and Roundcube can both
run without colliding.

apps.title: LAN file sharing (SMB + DLNA)
apps.description:
Samba exports the media root over SMB for computers/phones.
MiniDLNA advertises the same content over UPnP/DLNA for smart TVs
and consoles that don't speak SMB.
apps.compose:
# aurora.local / packages/storage
#
# LAN file sharing. Samba exports the media root over SMB. MiniDLNA
# advertises the same content over UPnP/DLNA for smart TVs that
# don't speak SMB.

name: aurora-storage

networks:
  aurora_net:
    external: true

services:
  samba:
    image: dockurr/samba:latest
    container_name: samba
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [aurora_net]
    ports:
      - "445:445"
    # dockurr/samba is env-var configured for a single share (NAME/USER/
    # PASS/RW/UID/GID). That covers this package exactly, because storage
    # only ever defined one share ("media") — dperson/samba's repeatable
    # `-s` scheme was never actually exercised beyond one entry. A second
    # share would need the image's mounted smb.conf/users.conf route
    # instead.
    #
    # No nmbd/wsdd/Avahi in this image (its only two installed packages
    # are samba and libauth-samba) — the host's own avahi-daemon handles
    # mDNS for aurora.local, and a container-side responder would have
    # fought it for UDP 5353. That is why port 139 (NetBIOS) is dropped
    # here too: this image runs smbd only, so nothing listens on it.
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ:-Europe/London}
      - NAME=media
      - USER=${SAMBA_USER:-bruce}
      - PASS=${SAMBA_PASS:-changeme}
      - UID=1000
      - GID=1000
      - RW=true
    volumes:
      - /home/bruce/media:/storage

  minidlna:
    image: vladgh/minidlna:latest
    container_name: minidlna
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      - MINIDLNA_MEDIA_DIR=/media
      - MINIDLNA_FRIENDLY_NAME=aurora.local
    volumes:
      - /home/bruce/media:/media:ro
      - ../../data/minidlna:/minidlna
apps.env_example:
# aurora.local / packages/storage / .env

TZ=Europe/London

# Samba credentials for the media share.
SAMBA_USER=bruce
SAMBA_PASS=changeme
apps.readme:
# storage

LAN file sharing over SMB (Samba) and DLNA (MiniDLNA).

The media root (`$MEDIA_ROOT` from `group_vars/all.yml`) is exported
read-only by default.

## First-run

1. `./scripts/up.sh storage`
2. Windows: `\\<hostname>.local\media`
3. macOS Finder: **Go → Connect to Server → `smb://<hostname>.local`**
4. DLNA appears automatically on smart TVs/consoles.
